builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: PagedMoE: Cross-Precision Expert Caching for Token-Level Dynamic Precision in SSD-Resident MoE Inference
summary: PagedMoE replaces storing each bit-width of an SSD-resident MoE expert as an independent cache object with a single prefix-compatible tree-codebook and bitplane layout, so cached low-precision data is reused and only missing bitplanes are fetched for higher precision. It costs a custom storage format, direct execution on 1-8-bit prefixes, and offline per-expert error profiles to select prefix length before I/O. It can fail if the routing-weight-based precision selection misestimates importance on out-of-distribution inputs, and the reported gains are demonstrated only on very large MoE models that require SSD offloading, so benefits may vanish for models that already fit in DRAM.
rationale: The technique directly targets the reader's constraint of running large MoE models on a single 24 GB GPU via SSD offloading, but it requires a specialized inference stack and workload-specific validation of the precision-selection policy before production reliance.
technique: Prefix-compatible cross-precision expert caching for SSD-resident MoE

claims.statement: PagedMoE replaces storing each bit-width of an SSD-resident MoE expert as an independent cache object with a single prefix-compatible tree-codebook and bitplane layout, so cached low-precision data is reused and only missing bitplanes are fetched for higher precision. It costs a custom storage format, direct execution on 1-8-bit prefixes, and offline per-expert error profiles to select prefix length before I/O. It can fail if the routing-weight-based precision selection misestimates importance on out-of-distribution inputs, and the reported gains are demonstrated only on very large MoE models that require SSD offloading, so benefits may vanish for models that already fit in DRAM.

At an average routed-expert precision of 2.5 bits with a 24 GiB expert cache, PagedMoE reaches 8.89 tokens/s on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, 1.33x the throughput of independent-precision caching and 1.56x that of uniform 4-bit execution, with quality close to GPTQ-INT4.
